landmarks.name: Rusizi National Park
landmarks.writeup: A protected area known for its hippos, crocodiles, and diverse bird species along the Rusizi River.

wiki.extract:
Rusizi National Park is a national park in Burundi, next to the Rusizi River.
It is 15 km north of the city of Bujumbura and home to hippopotamuses and sitatungas. Gustave, a Nile crocodile, is rumored to have killed 300 people here.

landmarks.name: Gishora Drum Sanctuary
landmarks.writeup: A cultural site preserving the traditional Burundian drumming heritage, central to national identity.

wiki.extract: The field of Gishora is located approximately 7 km north of the city of Gitega, in the Gitega Province of Burundi. It houses a royal palace and royal field.

landmarks.name: Lake Tanganyika
landmarks.writeup: One of the African Great Lakes, it is the second deepest freshwater lake in the world and vital for fishing.

wiki.extract: Lake Tanganyika is an African Great Lake. It is the world's second-largest freshwater lake by volume and the second deepest, in both cases after Lake Baikal in Siberia. It is the world's longest freshwater lake. It is also the 6th largest lake by area. The lake is shared among four countries—Tanzania, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, and Zambia—with Tanzania (46%) and the DRC (40%) possessing the majority of the lake. It drains via the Lukuga River into the Congo River system, which ultimately discharges at Banana, Democratic Republic of the Congo into the Atlantic Ocean.

cultural_events.name: Umuganuro Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A traditional harvest festival celebrating the start of the agricultural season with music and dance.

wiki.extract: The karyenda is a traditional African drum. It was the main symbol of Burundi and its Mwami (King) and had semi-divine status. The Mwami was said to interpret the beatings of the karyenda into rules for the kingdom.

cultural_events.name: National Drummers Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An event showcasing Burundi's famous drumming culture, featuring performances from local and national groups.

wiki.extract: John Henry Bonham was an English musician who was the drummer of the rock band Led Zeppelin. Noted for his speed, power, fast single-footed kick drumming, distinctive sound, and feel for groove, he is regarded as one of the greatest and most influential drummers in history.

food_writeup: Burundian cuisine is based on staple foods like beans, maize, sweet potatoes, and bananas, often accompanied by meat or fish. Ugali (a maize porridge) and isombe (cassava leaves) are popular dishes.
brief_history: Burundi, once part of the Kingdom of Burundi, became a German colony in the late 19th century, then a Belgian mandate after WWI. It gained independence in 1962. The country has experienced ethnic conflicts and civil war but continues efforts toward peace and development.
current_conflicts: Burundi faces political tensions and occasional unrest related to governance and human rights issues, but no active large-scale armed conflict.

commentary.inflation_management: Burundi's inflation history is one of repeated loss of control. It ran at 24.4% in 2008 during the global food-fuel crisis, then moderated to single digits through the early 2010s, even turning to deflation in 2018 (-2.8%) and 2019 (-0.8%). The current crisis is worse: a severe foreign-exchange shortage, monetized deficits, and a collapsing parallel exchange rate pushed inflation to 18.9% in 2022, 27.1% in 2023, 20.2% in 2024, and a series high of 34.2% projected for 2025. The central bank has devalued the franc in steps but remains far from a market-clearing rate, so inflation expectations are unanchored and basic goods are chronically scarce.
commentary.debt_management: Burundi's debt was transformed by HIPC/MDRI relief: from a crushing 130.3% of GDP in 2006, completion-point relief brought it down to 25.7% by 2009. Since then it has crept back up through fiscal deficits and donor withdrawal after the 2015 crisis, reaching 69.8% in 2022 before easing to a projected 41.2% in 2025 as the denominator recovered. The debt is mostly concessional and domestic, so near-term solvency is not the issue; the issue is that borrowing has financed consumption and the security apparatus rather than productive investment, while arrears to the private sector accumulate.

key_events.event: HIPC completion-point debt relief cut public debt from 130.3% (2006) to 25.7% of GDP.
President Nkurunziza's bid for a third term triggered protests, a failed coup, and a crackdown; donors suspended direct budget support, deepening the forex crisis.
Nkurunziza died in office; Evariste Ndayishimiye succeeded him, with modest diplomatic re-engagement.
Ukraine war and forex shortages pushed inflation to 27.1%; the central bank devalued the franc.
Inflation projected at 34.2%, the series high, amid continued parallel-market depreciation and goods shortages.

commentary.outlook_next_decade: The base case is continued stagflation: without a credible exchange-rate adjustment and restored donor relations, inflation will stay high and growth too low to reduce poverty. Upside depends on genuine forex liberalization and agricultural recovery; downside is a full-blown currency crisis. Uncertainty is high: the political system is stable but closed, and economic data quality is weak, so even the direction of travel is hard to verify.
commentary.caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
